difficulty.from: engine meta: closest gap 2 degrees, misleading arm lengths

answer.line: Smallest to largest, the angles are 23, 25, 31 and 34 degrees: 2, 4, 1, 3.

steps: Read the choices first. They start with 2 or 4 and end with 1 or 3, so two close calls decide it.
Angle 2 against 4: 23 against 25. The long arms on 2 make it look bigger; judge the corner.
Angle 1 against 3: 31 against 34. The short arms on 3 make it look smaller.
Two choices survive. 4 against 1 is 6 degrees apart, the easy call, so 2-4-1-3.

choices.note: Angles 2 and 4 differ by 2 degrees, 23 against 25. The long arms on angle 2 make it look like the bigger one.
Angle 3 is 34 degrees and angle 1 is 31. The short arms on angle 3 make it look smaller than it is.
Angle 4 is 25 degrees and angle 1 is 31, the widest gap in the set. This swap comes from settling the ends and then rushing the middle.

lockIt: Rank by the opening at the vertex, never arm length. Let the choices tell you which close calls matter.
